A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer-based Bayesian inference study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original posterior-inference experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, including GLM, factor-analysis, and Gaussian-mixture results, runtimes, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds predictive evaluations, Gaussian and score-matching comparisons, dimensionality studies, and classifier-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The encoder, conditional flow-matching decoder, synthetic training framework, and ODE sampling procedure remain. However, v2 removes the denominator from the printed flow-matching target and gives inconsistent signs in Equations (5) and (7). The PDFs do not establish whether these equation edits reflect an implemented loss change or corrections to its description.

E1.justification: The same tabular benchmark and seven GLM, six FA, and four GMM scenarios remain. v2 adds downstream regression and classification prediction evaluations in Appendix J and additional prior-shift conditions in Figure 9. No new dataset collection or application domain is introduced; the dimensionality extensions primarily change experimental settings.

E2.justification: v2 adds MAP and TabPFN to predictive comparisons, a forward-KL Gaussian in-context learner in Appendix K, and score-matching diffusion in Appendix L.2. These substantially broaden the evaluated alternatives. Laplace, the four VI methods, HMC, SGLD, MLP encoders, and diffusion paths learned through flow matching were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate posterior-mean predictions using RMSE or accuracy, extend GLMs to 20 and 50 dimensions, compare neural-network and random-forest C2ST classifiers, and quantify distribution shifts using C2ST. The dimensionality experiments use only five real-world datasets at 20 dimensions and one at 50. The original benchmark protocol and training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds Gaussian-posterior and score-matching ablations, systematic dimensionality sensitivity, classifier-choice validation, and a distribution-gap analysis in Figure 9. These investigate posterior parametrization, conditioning failures, scaling, and metric dependence. The earlier MLP, learning-rate, diffusion-path, and mild OOD analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report uncertainties and use two-standard-error highlighting, while retaining the footnote describing significance using two standard deviations. v2 documents no new seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedure. Additional uncertainty values accompany new results without establishing a changed reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the matched earlier appendix tables retain their numerical results. v2 adds substantial predictive, Gaussian-approximation, score-matching, dimensionality, OOD, and neural-network C2ST results. For example, Table 15 reports GLM scenario 2 real-world RMSE of 0.561 for ICL versus 0.449 for TabPFN; Tables 36–41 reveal weaker relative performance at higher dimensions. These are newly reported evaluations, not improvements to the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Section 3.1.2 adds explicit density and probability-path representation assumptions. The flow-matching discrepancy and empirical-loss formulas also change beyond equivalent notation: the earlier target denominator disappears, while v2 Equation (7) has signs inconsistent with Equation (5). Proposition 1 remains unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claims that transformers can learn full posterior inference and compete with established inference methods remain. v2 adds systematic objective, robustness, and dimensionality ablations as an explicit fifth contribution and clarifies that the learned mapping concerns a specific probabilistic model. The headline contribution is not replaced.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications concerning higher-dimensional failures, metric saturation, and the distinction between posterior similarity and predictive performance. It also proposes that noisy score-matching objectives can cause the model to ignore conditioning and emphasizes that experiments concern relatively simple posteriors. These extend v1's existing computational-cost and misspecification limitations.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states that a separate model is trained from scratch for each scenario and identifies methodological setup references for the diffusion and neural-network C2ST comparisons. The existing architecture sizes, optimizer settings, synthetic-data budget, hardware, ODE tolerances, preprocessing, and code location are retained. The changes mainly improve disclosure rather than document a revised implementation.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive positioning against concurrent Mittal studies, inference compilation by Le et al., and TabPFN-based posterior sampling by Vetter et al. New Appendix E distinguishes posterior sampling from explicit density estimation and discusses several additional approaches. This substantially expands the research context beyond isolated citation updates.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative and appendices: realistic-data generation moves from the main text to Appendix B, preprocessing and background move earlier, and detailed results move to Appendix I. New Section 4.4 summarizes the diagnostic experiments. Much existing prose remains, but its organization and explanatory framing change considerably.

P2.justification: The main paper adopts a two-column conference layout with compact, reformatted summary tables. Figure 3 is reduced from six marginal columns to four, architecture captions expand, and existing figures and tables are relocated. New density and OOD plots and substantial new comparison-table structures further change the presentation.

improvement.justification: The added dimensionality and predictive studies make applicability limits clearer, while Gaussian and score-matching ablations strengthen examination of the design choices. These provide useful diagnostic evidence beyond v1's retained benchmarks. However, inconsistent loss signs in Equations (5) and (7), conflicting repeated RF values in Table 45, and impossible ROC-AUC values such as 1.012 in Table 47 weaken parts of the revision. The clearer limitations support a limited net improvement, tempered by these reporting defects.
